title: Corporate Airlines 5966
summary: Corporate Airlines Flight 5966, a British Aerospace Jetstream 32 twin-engine turboprop with 15 aboard (2 crew, 13 passengers), crashed on approach to Kirksville Regional Airport near Pettis Township, Missouri on October 19, 2004. Captain Kim Sasse and First Officer Jonathan Palmer conducted a non-precision instrument approach at night in instrument meteorological conditions. The pilots descended below minimum descent altitude into a region without guaranteed obstacle clearance, struck trees, and crashed. Both pilots and 11 of 13 passengers were killed. The NTSB determined that the pilots' failure to follow established procedures for non-precision instrument approaches, specifically their descent below MDA before required visual cues, combined with crew fatigue from a 14-hour duty day, inadequate monitoring by the first officer, and breakdown in crew resource management were the probable causes.
probable_cause: Pilots' failure to follow established procedures and properly conduct non-precision instrument approach at night in IMC, specifically their descent below minimum descent altitude before required visual cues were available, and their failure to maintain established division of duties between flying and monitoring pilots. Contributing factors: crew fatigue from 14-hour duty day and failure to make standard callouts.

factors.evidence: Pilots descended below minimum descent altitude before required visual cues were available, continuing unmoderated until aircraft struck trees during approach in IMC.
Both pilots were looking outside cockpit for visual cues rather than monitoring instruments; first officer did not challenge captain to maintain instrument scan.
First officer failed to challenge captain and maintain professional monitoring duties; failure to establish professional demeanor during flight.
Pilots had worked 14-hour duty day including six flights, degrading performance despite regulations last updated in 1964.
Pilots failed to follow established procedures and make standard callouts during non-precision approach.
Night instrument meteorological conditions with no visual references to airport or terrain.
Aircraft struck trees during descent on approach and crashed near Kirksville.

events.text: October 19, 2004: Flight 5966 operated by Corporate Airlines (RegionsAir) departed St. Louis Lambert on evening for Kirksville; crew had completed six flights on 14-hour duty day
Aircraft cleared for non-precision instrument approach to Kirksville in night IMC conditions
Captain Sasse began looking outside cockpit for visual cues to runway location
Captain continued descent below MDA; first officer did not challenge or call attention to descent rate or failed instrument scan
Aircraft struck trees and crashed during continued unmoderated descent below minimum descent altitude near Kirksville Regional Airport; 13 of 15 persons killed

notes: Report focused on cockpit voice recorder analysis showing crew procedures and communication breakdown
Probable cause clear: descent below MDA combined with fatigue and CRM breakdown
Summary record contained detailed CRM analysis and fatigue contribution
Depth set to 'sections' due to focus on CVR analysis rather than detailed technical investigation
